import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 19.25

by B. Curtin, G. R. Pourgholi

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
-/

open scoped Nat Group

namespace Kourovka.«19.25»

/--
Let $G$ and $H$ be finite groups of the same order with
$\sum_{g \in G} \phi(|g|) = \sum_{h \in H} \phi(|h|)$,
where $\phi$ is the Euler totient function. Suppose that $G$ is simple. Is
$H$ necessarily simple?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka_19_25 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H] [Fintype G] [Fintype H],
       Fintype.card G = Fintype.card H →
       ∑ g : G, φ (orderOf g) = ∑ h : H, φ (orderOf h) →
       IsSimpleGroup G → IsSimpleGroup H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«19.25»

status_issues.source_status: Solved negatively by Pietro Monticone in 2026. The latest Kourovka Notebook credits his solution and also cites van Doorn, Judin, Monticone and Morrison, arXiv:2607.17477 (July 2026).
status_issues.evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/1401.0300v46#p1030 explicitly adds: “No, it need not be (P. Monticone, Preprint, 2026 …)”. Section 4 of arXiv:2607.17477 constructs G = PSU(3,3) and H = C₆ × S₄ × (C₇ ⋊ C₆), where a generator of C₆ acts on C₇ by multiplication by 3 modulo 7. Both have order 6048 and totient sum 23984, but G is simple and H is not. The paper’s bibliography dates Monticone’s original solution note to 10 May 2026.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to research solved and replace answer(sorry) with answer(False). Keep the right-hand proposition unchanged and add a reference to the negative solution.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states Problem 19.25 as posed in the cited v40 source. Quantifier scope, both equalities, and the simplicity implication agree. Fintype excludes infinite groups; group structure excludes empty carriers; orderOf is positive on every permitted element, so its infinite-order default cannot affect the sum. IsSimpleGroup uses the standard nontrivial-group convention. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings and checks these boundaries, cyclic-group sums for orders 1–4, simplicity at small prime orders, and invariance of the sum under group isomorphism. It also verifies the arithmetic of the published counterexample’s order-distribution tables, not the full counterexample construction.
